submission.justification:
Simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c: R3 peaks near 2 cm (4.45σ; 4.40σ at 3 cm, 3.22σ at 6 cm), R1 rises to 3.83σ at 3 cm (3.63σ at 2 cm, 2.67σ at 6 cm), R2 is lowest (2.02σ at 6 cm). R3 gives roughly 0.6σ more separation, but it is a porous radiator with no hydrophobic treatment, and R1 is the porous option with hydrophobic treatment, which is the mitigation most relevant to the hard humidity-ageing limit. No project document or tool provides humidity-ageing transparency data for any candidate, so the 10% transparency-loss constraint cannot be verified for R1 or R3. I chose R1 at 3 cm as the lower-risk option given that hard, non-replaceable constraint, accepting the performance cost. Before procurement, a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must be run on R1 (and R3 if its performance advantage is to be reconsidered). If R1 fails that test, R2 (solid, lower index) is the likely fallback, but it has the weakest separation.</justification>
